questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct statement about paths and cycles in a graph?

choices.A: A path always starts and ends at different vertices.
choices.B: A cycle has no repeated vertices except for the starting and ending vertex.
choices.C: A path can have repeated vertices but not repeated edges.
choices.D: A cycle is a path with at least one repeated edge.

questions.solution: A cycle is a path that starts and ends at the same vertex and has at least one repeated edge. Option A is incorrect because paths do not necessarily start and end at different vertices. Option B is wrong because cycles have repeated vertices other than the starting and ending vertex. Option C is false because paths cannot have repeated edges.
questions.explanation: This question tests understanding of the basic definitions of paths and cycles in graph theory.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Confusing a path with a cycle, thinking that paths can start and end at the same vertex or cycles do not allow repeated vertices other than the starting and ending one.

questions.stem: In an undirected graph, which of the following statements is true about a path between two vertices?

choices.A: The path must be a straight line.
choices.B: Each edge can only be traversed in one direction.
choices.C: There can be multiple distinct paths between the vertices.
choices.D: Every vertex on the path must have an even degree.

questions.solution: In an undirected graph, there can be multiple distinct paths between two vertices. Option A is incorrect because paths in graphs do not necessarily follow straight lines. Option B is false because edges in an undirected graph can be traversed in both directions. Option D is wrong because vertex degree has no direct relation to the existence of a path.
questions.explanation: This question assesses understanding of path properties in undirected graphs.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Assuming that paths in undirected graphs follow specific rules, such as straight lines or single-direction edges.

questions.stem: In a directed graph, which of the following statements is true about cycles?

choices.A: A cycle must have an odd number of vertices.
choices.B: A cycle can have parallel edges between two vertices.
choices.C: Every vertex in the cycle must have both incoming and outgoing edges.
choices.D: There can be multiple disconnected cycles in a directed graph.

questions.solution: In a directed graph, there can be multiple disconnected cycles. Option A is incorrect because cycles do not necessarily have an odd number of vertices. Option B is false because parallel edges are not allowed in cycles (they would form a loop instead). Option C is wrong because it's possible for a vertex in a cycle to only have incoming or outgoing edges.
questions.explanation: This question tests knowledge of cycles in directed graphs.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Assuming that cycles in directed graphs follow specific rules, such as having an odd number of vertices or requiring both incoming and outgoing edges for each vertex.

questions.stem: In a simple graph, what is the minimum number of edges required to form a path between two vertices?
questions.solution: A path in a simple graph requires at least 2 edges to connect two vertices. One edge connects the starting vertex to another, and the second edge connects that vertex to the destination vertex.
questions.explanation: This question checks understanding of the minimum requirements for forming a path in a graph.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Assuming that only one edge is needed to form a path between two vertices.

questions.stem: What is the minimum number of edges required to form a cycle in a simple graph?
questions.solution: A cycle in a simple graph requires at least 3 edges to form a closed loop connecting three vertices.
questions.explanation: This question tests the understanding of the minimum requirements for forming a cycle in a graph.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Assuming that only two edges are needed to form a cycle, which would actually create a line rather than a closed loop.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates a path from a loop in a graph?

choices.A: Paths have no repeated vertices, while loops can repeat vertices.
choices.B: Loops always start and end at the same vertex, while paths do not.
choices.C: Paths can have parallel edges, but loops cannot.
choices.D: Loops have an odd number of edges, while paths can have any number.

questions.solution: Loops always start and end at the same vertex, while paths do not necessarily connect the same starting and ending vertices. Option A is incorrect because paths can have repeated vertices (as long as they are not back- to-back). Option C is false because both paths and loops cannot have parallel edges. Option D is wrong because loop edge count has no specific rule.
questions.explanation: This question assesses understanding of the differences between paths and loops in graphs.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Confusing loops with cycles or thinking that paths cannot repeat vertices.

questions.stem: In a connected graph, which of the following statements is true?

choices.A: Every vertex must be part of a cycle.
choices.B: There can be multiple disconnected cycles in the graph.
choices.C: There exists at least one path between any two vertices.
choices.D: The graph must have an odd number of edges.

questions.solution: In a connected graph, there must exist at least one path between any two vertices. Option A is incorrect because not all vertices in a connected graph need to be part of a cycle. Option B is false because multiple disconnected cycles would mean the graph is not connected. Option D is wrong because the number of edges has no specific rule for connectivity.
questions.explanation: This question tests knowledge of connectivity properties in graphs.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Assuming that all vertices must be part of a cycle or that multiple disconnected cycles are allowed in a connected graph.
